learning_outcomes.text: The meaning of the fundamental physical concepts concerning the principles of the mechanics of the point mass.
The ability to apply such principles in solving simple physical problems.

syllabus_topics: Physical quantities and their measurements: units and dimensions
Position, velocity, and acceleration vectors in Cartesian coordinates, polar coordinates, and intrinsic representation
Study of some simple problems of dynamics of the point mass (motion with elastic force, projectile motion, simple pendulum, motion with friction forces, gravitational force)
Examples: calculation of the potential of weight force, elastic force, gravitational force
The third Principle of dynamics (conservation of momentum and angular momentum)
Brief outlines of the dynamics of the rigid body
Brief outlines of the structure of matter
Definition of electric field and its vector aspects: field lines, field sources
Gauss's law in integral and differential form
The electric field as a conservative field: the electrostatic potential
Electrostatic energy density associated with the electric field
Energy of a system of point charges and a continuous charge distribution
Brief outlines of the electric dipole
Conductors in equilibrium, hollow conductors, field and charges on the surface of the conductor
Capacity calculations: plane, cylindrical, and spherical capacitor
Brief outlines of electrostatics with dielectrics
Definition of current intensity and unit of measure
The two Ohm's laws: resistance and resistivity
Magnetic fields in vacuum in the stationary case
Gauss's law for the magnetic field
Laplace's second law: magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor
Lorentz force on a moving charge
Magnetic dipole moment of the coil
Potential energy of the coil in an external magnetic field
Equivalence between the current-carrying coil and a permanent magnet
Stationary magnetic fields generated by currents
Laplace's first law or Biot-Savart: magnetic field generated by a current
Calculations of magnetic fields produced by elementary circuits
Magnetic field in an indefinite solenoid
Properties of the magnetic field in vacuum
Discussion of Maxwell's equations in integral and differential form
Brief outlines of electromagnetic waves and the energetic aspects of the electromagnetic field
teaching_methods: Lectures devoted to the presentation of theoretical foundations
Classroom problem-solving sessions focused on the quantitative application of physical laws
Integrated use of slides, digital whiteboards, and traditional blackboards
Guided discussion of representative examples and problems

assessment_methods.method: Mandatory written examination (4 numerical problems, 2 open-ended theoretical questions)

assessment_rules: The written examination is passed with a minimum score of 18/30 and a maximum of 27/30. Students who pass the written examination may register the mark or take an optional oral examination. The oral examination can increase or decrease the written mark by up to 5 points. The oral examination must be taken within the same session as the written examination.
